Tutorial: Test for etiologic heterogeneity in a case-control study

Emily C. Zabor

Last updated: October 15, 2026

Source: vignettes/eh_test.Rmd
eh_test.Rmd

Introduction

In epidemiologic studies polytomous logistic regression is commonly used in the study of etiologic heterogeneity when data are from a case-control study, and the method has good statistical properties. Although polytomous logistic regression can be implemented using available software, the additional calculations needed to perform a thorough analysis of etiologic heterogeneity are cumbersome. To facilitate use of this method we provide functions eh_test_subtype() and eh_test_marker() to address two key questions regarding etiologic heterogeneity:

  1. Do risk factor effects differ according to disease subtypes?
  2. Do risk factor effects differ according to individual disease markers that combine to form disease subtypes?

Whether disease subtypes are pre-specified or formed by cross-classification of individual disease markers, the resulting polytomous logistic regression model is the same. Let ii index study subjects, i=1,…,Ni = 1, \ldots, N, let mm index disease subtypes, m=0,…Mm = 0, \ldots M, where m=0m=0 denotes control subjects, and let pp index risk factors, p=1,…,Pp = 1, \ldots, P. The polytomous logistic regression model is specified as

Pr⁡(Y=m|𝑿)=exp⁡(𝑿T𝜷⋅m)𝟏+exp⁡(𝑿T𝜷)𝟏\Pr(Y = m | \mathbf{X}) = \frac{\exp(\mathbf{X}^T \boldsymbol{\beta}_{\boldsymbol{\cdot} m})}{\mathbf{1} + \exp(\mathbf{X}^T \boldsymbol{\beta}) \mathbf{1}} where 𝑿\mathbf{X} is the (P+1)×N(P+1) \times N matrix of risk factor values, with the first row all ones for the intercept, and 𝜷\boldsymbol{\beta} is the (P+1)×M(P+1) \times M matrix of regression coefficients. 𝜷⋅m\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\boldsymbol{\cdot} m} indicates the mmth column of the matrix 𝜷\boldsymbol{\beta} and 𝟏\mathbf{1} represents a vector of ones of length MM.

Pre-specified subtypes

If disease subtypes are pre-specified, either based on clustering high-dimensional disease marker data or based on a single disease marker or combinations of disease markers, then statistical tests for etiologic heterogeneity according to each risk factor can be conducted using the eh_test_subtype() function.

Estimates of the parameters of interest related to the question of whether risk factor effects differ across subtypes of disease, 𝜷̂\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}, and the associated estimated variance-covariance matrix, cov̂(𝜷̂)\widehat{cov}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}), are obtained directly from the resulting polytomous logistic regression model. Each βpm\beta_{pm} parameter represents the log odds ratio for a one-unit change in risk factor pp for subtype mm disease versus controls. Hypothesis tests for the question of whether a specific risk factor effect differs across subtypes of disease can be conducted separately for each risk factor pp using a Wald test of the hypothesis

H0βp.:βp1=…=βpMH_{0_{\beta_{p.}}}: \beta_{p1} = \dots = \beta_{pM} Using the subtype_data simulated dataset, we can examine the influence of risk factors x1, x2, and x3 on the 4 pre-specified disease subtypes in variable subtype using the following code:

library(riskclustr)

mod1 <- eh_test_subtype(
  label = "subtype", 
  M = 4, 
  factors = list("x1", "x2", "x3"), 
  data = subtype_data)

See the function documentation for details of function arguments.

The resulting estimates 𝜷̂\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} can be accessed with

mod1$beta

Subtypes formed by cross-classification of disease markers

If disease subtypes are formed by cross-classifying individual binary disease markers, then statistical tests for associations between risk factors and individual disease markers can be conducted using the eh_test_marker() funtion.

Let kk index disease markers, k=1,…,Kk = 1, \ldots, K. Here the MM disease subtypes are formed by cross-classification of the KK binary disease markers, so that we have M=2KM = 2^K disease subtypes.

To evaluate the independent influences of individual disease markers, it is convenient to transform the parameters in 𝜷\boldsymbol{\beta} using the one-to-one linear transformation

𝜸̂=𝜷̂𝑳M/2.\hat{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} = \frac{\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \mathbf{L}}{M/2}. Here 𝑳\mathbf{L} is an M×KM \times K contrast matrix such that the entries are -1 if disease marker kk is absent for disease subtype mm and 1 if disease marker kk is present for disease subtype mm. 𝜸\boldsymbol{\gamma} is then the (P+1)×K(P+1) \times K matrix of parameters that reflect the independent effects of distinct disease markers. Each element of the 𝜸\boldsymbol{\gamma} parameters represents the average of differences in log odds ratios between disease subtypes defined by different levels of the kkth disease marker with respect to the ppth risk factor when the other disease markers are held constant. Variance estimates corresponding to each γ̂pk\hat{\gamma}_{pk} are obtained using

var̂(γ̂pk)=(M2)−2𝑳⋅kTcov̂(𝜷̂p⋅T)𝑳⋅k\widehat{var}(\hat{\gamma}_{pk}) = \left(\frac{M}{2}\right)^{-2} \mathbf{L}_{\boldsymbol{\cdot} k}^T \widehat{cov}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{p \boldsymbol{\cdot}}^T) \mathbf{L}_{\boldsymbol{\cdot} k} where 𝑳⋅k\mathbf{L}_{\boldsymbol{\cdot} k} is the kkth column of the 𝑳\mathbf{L} matrix and the estimated variance-covariance matrix cov̂(𝜷̂p⋅)\widehat{cov}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{p \boldsymbol{\cdot}}) for each risk factor pp is obtained directly from the polytomous logistic regression model.

Hypothesis tests for the question of whether a risk factor effect differs across levels of each individual disease marker of which the disease subtypes are comprised can be conducted separately for each combination of risk factor pp and disease marker kk using a Wald test of the hypothesis

H0γpk:γpk=0.H_{0_{{\gamma_{pk}}}}: \gamma_{pk} = 0. Using the subtype_data simulated dataset, we can examine the influence of risk factors x1, x2, and x3 on the two individual disease markers marker1 and marker2. These two binary disease markers will be cross-classified to form four disease subtypes that will be used as the outcome in the polytomous logistic regression model to obtain the 𝜷̂\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} estimates, which are then transformed in order to obtain estimates and hypothesis tests related to the individual disease markers.

library(riskclustr)

mod2 <- eh_test_marker(
  markers = list("marker1", "marker2"),
  factors = list("x1", "x2", "x3"),
  case = "case",
  data = subtype_data)

See the function documentation for details of function arguments.

The resulting estimates 𝜸̂\hat{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} can be accessed with
